item.description:
## Board releases and tags
Cards can now belong to a release version. Create versions, assign a card to one from its detail view, and filter the board by one or several releases, including cards with no release. Released versions are grouped apart in the menus and can be hidden. Tags can be defined, assigned to cards, filtered on and colored. The board remembers your filters for each workspace.
- Threads started for a worktree get a board card automatically. - A card's model shows as an icon on the card, and the thread's board column shows as a live pill instead of in its title. - Clicking a card selects its linked thread and shows the transcript. The board has new Open Issues and Fixing columns. - Every column's prompt now starts a thread bound to its card.
## Fixes
- Reading the board, or using the search and skill tools, no longer makes a planning thread move its card to In Progress. - Subthread instructions that an agent writes now show in green like the ones you write. - The Review panel shows Auto Fix status and Stop only for the thread that owns the run, so another thread's fix no longer looks like it is blocking yours. - Queued builds and tests now run in the order the agent asked for them, and finished test runs no longer freeze the app while they are processed. - The panel keeps its width after you close and reopen it.

## Kanban task board
A new Board tab shows your workspace's tasks as cards in columns. Turn it on from the tab, then add, edit, reorder and move cards by drag or from a menu. Cards can carry notes and subtasks, and the tab has a card filter, per-column sorting, and show/hide for columns.
- Moving a card follows the work. A thread started for a card moves it to In Progress, then In Review when its pull request opens, then Done when it merges. Cards show a git status icon and the pull request number. - A column can run a prompt on an agent whenever a card arrives, and you can give a column or a task its own model. - Agents can read the board, edit and move cards, and ask you to delete one. Nothing is deleted until you click Delete on that card. - Import tasks from a tracker file or a folder of them. The agent proposes cards and nothing is added until you approve the batch.
## Threads can move to their own branch
An agent working on the default branch can now move its thread onto a new branch in its own worktree, without starting a separate subthread.
## Fixes and review
- A subthread request you have accepted keeps going when the agent's turn ends. Antigravity ends its turn while a spawn is still running, which used to cancel it and leave a stray branch behind. Antigravity also gets Kulula's tools directly in its tool list. - Auto Commit/Push after a Fix now tells you in the thread why it did not run. - Findings no longer get stuck on "fixing" after a fix turn is refused or interrupted, so Fix and Auto Fix can retry them. - A review panel refresh no longer erases the "fixed" status an Auto Fix run just recorded.
## Look and feel
Engines now show vector logos instead of text glyphs, and errors and warnings in the review panel tabs share one alert style.

## Actions tab
A new Actions tab keeps your saved prompts in one place so you can run them again without retyping.
## Plan usage
Usage now shows what you have remaining rather than what you have used. The Status tab also shows your Codex weekly quota with progress bars, and Codex usage refreshes on its own.
## Model defaults in Settings
Settings now has multi-level model and effort selectors, so you can set a default for each action.
## Build and test results reach the agent
When a build or test run finishes in the queue, the result goes back to the agent that asked for it. A finished thread can also start a subthread without being told to.
## Fewer stalls
A held process tree no longer stops the build queue, and Kulula warns you when a merge leaves the worktree in place. Rate and spending limit errors from Codex now show the reason instead of a generic failure.
## Local review
Local review now refreshes the pull request head first, so it reviews the latest commits.
